chief_complaint: rapid monocular visual loss over days accompanied by eye pain worsening with eye movement and central scotoma in young woman
hpi_details: 29F presents with acute right-eye vision reduction to 20/200, pain behind the eye on movement, a central scotoma, and a strong right relative afferent pupillary defect with a normal optic disc. Urgent MRI of the brain and orbits shows demyelinating plaques; ophthalmology/neurology will determine whether high-dose IV methylprednisolone is appropriate.
ideas: She thinks she pulled an eye muscle from working on screens or developed a deep sinus infection pressing on the back of her eye.
concerns: She is worried that a tumor is growing behind her eye socket that will permanently steal her eyesight.
expectations: She hopes to get an urgent brain scan today and start medication that will quickly restore her sight before her work week starts.

available_results.test: MRI brain and orbits with contrast
available_results.value: Right optic nerve enhancement and multiple periventricular ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions compatible with demyelination

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Optic neuritis (possible multiple sclerosis presentation).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Ischemic optic neuropathy without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Pain with eye movement.

teaching.one_liner: 29F with rapid monocular vision loss over days, pain with eye movement, central scotoma, and a positive RAPD.

must_ask.say: Does it hurt when you move your eye from side to side?

must_ask.objective: Ask about the pattern and rate of vision loss
must_ask.say: How quickly did your vision decline — over hours, days?
Have you had any numbness, weakness, or balance problems elsewhere in your body?
Do colors look washed out or less vivid in the affected eye?

must_ask.objective: Explain MRI and steroid treatment plan
must_ask.say: We need urgent MRI of the brain and eye sockets to look for inflammation or demyelination; the eye and neurology teams will discuss whether IV steroids are appropriate.

history.answer: My right eye has gotten really blurry over the last three days, and it aches deep behind the eye whenever I move it.
It started about three days ago with a dull ache behind my right eye, and my vision has progressively gotten darker and cloudier each day.
It is only my right eye. When I cover my right eye, my left eye sees completely clearly.
The blurriness is constant throughout the day; it does not come and go or flicker back to normal.
There is a dark smudge right in the center of my vision in that eye, while I can see slightly better around the edges.
Yes, colors look completely washed out and dull through my right eye, especially bright red objects.
Both near and far vision are blurry in my right eye, and adjusting distance does not help at all.
I haven't noticed excessive glare or halos around lights, though bright lights feel slightly uncomfortable.
No, I haven't seen any floating specks, cobwebs, or flashing lights.
No, it does not look like a dark curtain falling over my eye; it is just a dark cloud right in the middle.
No, I am not seeing double images at all.
No, my eyelids are not drooping, and I have no trouble chewing, swallowing, or talking.
Yes, it is a deep, aching pain right behind my right eyeball that sharpens whenever I look up, down, or sideways.
No, there is no redness, crusting, or discharge coming from either eye.
No, I don't have a new severe headache, tenderness along my temples, or jaw cramping when I chew.
No, I have no weakness in my arms or legs, no numbness or tingling, and my speech is completely normal.
No, I haven't felt dizzy, unsteady, or lightheaded.
No, I haven't bumped my head or had any injury to my face or eyes.
No, I've never been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, or cholesterol problems.
No, I have never had heart palpitations, irregular heartbeats, or blood clots.
I only wear mild glasses for distance, and I have never had glaucoma, cataracts, or eye surgery.
No, I am not taking steroids, hydroxychloroquine, tuberculosis medications, or any other prescriptions.
I've stopped driving since it started because my depth perception is off, but I haven't fallen or tripped.
I thought maybe I severely strained an eye muscle at my desk or had a bad sinus blockage trapped behind my eye.
I'm terrified that there's a brain tumor or growth behind my eye that's going to leave me blind.
I was hoping to get an MRI done right away and some strong medicine to bring my vision back before Monday.
I have always been completely healthy with no chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I have no allergies to any medications, foods, or latex.
I don't smoke cigarettes, and I've never used tobacco or vape products.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine once or twice a month.
I work as a graphic designer in an office, and I live with my partner in a quiet apartment.
There is no family history of multiple sclerosis, glaucoma, macular degeneration, or autoimmune diseases.
My last period was two weeks ago, my monthly cycles are regular, and there is no chance I could be pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.

Visual acuity is 20/200 in the right eye with no pinhole improvement (20/20 in left eye), confrontation reveals a right central scotoma, swinging flashlight test demonstrates a marked right relative afferent pupillary defect, fundoscopy shows a normal optic disc without swelling, and extraocular movements elicit retrobulbar pain.
Bilateral superficial temporal arteries are non-tender, non-thickened, and normally pulsatile.
Cranial nerves III through XII are intact with normal facial sensation, symmetric facial movement, and no ptosis.
Normal muscle bulk and tone throughout, with 5/5 motor strength in all bilateral upper and lower extremity muscle groups.
Light touch, pinprick, vibration, and joint position sensation are intact and symmetric bilaterally.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric at the biceps, patellar, and Achilles tendons; plantar responses are flexor bilaterally.
Coordination on finger-to-nose and rapid alternating movements is intact, Romberg test is negative, and tandem gait is steady.
